short: Won Scotland's independence at Bannockburn after years as a fugitive king.
full:
Robert Bruce killed his rival John Comyn before the altar of the Greyfriars church at Dumfries in February 1306 and had himself crowned at Scone six weeks later, while Edward I was still alive. Defeated twice within months, excommunicated and driven into hiding in the western isles, he came back to fight a war of raids and sieges that took castle after castle from the English.

Edward II finally marched north in 1314 to relieve Stirling and lost decisively at Bannockburn on 23 and 24 June, where Scottish schiltrons broke English cavalry on boggy ground. Independence took longer to win on paper: the Declaration of Arbroath was sent to the pope in 1320, and English recognition came only with the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton in 1328. Robert died the following June, probably of leprosy, having asked that his heart be carried on crusade.
